newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kobe Steel says to form Thai steel processing unit.
newsitem.headline: Kobe Steel says to form Thai steel processing unit.

text.p: Kobe Steel Ltd said on Wednesday it plans to set up a joint venture in Bangkok, Thailand, to process steel wire rod used in making high quality automobile parts.
The joint venture, Kobe CH Wire (Thailand) Co Ltd, to be formed in September, will be capitalised at 56 million baht, or about 200 million yen.

It will be owned 33 percent by Kobe Steel, 25 percent by Kobe Steel's trading arm Shinsho Corp, 20 percent by Mahajak Autoparts, and 11 percent each by O & K Co Ltd, a Japanese steel wire processor, and Nissho Iwai Corp.
The new company will supply cold heading quality (CHQ) wire, a high-end product, to Japanese manufacturers of nuts and bolts in Thailand.
The venture will also enable local partner Mahajak Autoparts, a local manufacturer of automobile parts, to improve the quality of the nuts and bolts it produces, Kobe said in a statement.
The company will start operations in October with a capacity of 1,500 tonnes per month at a plant in Nongjok, Bangkok. Kobe Steel will supply the venture with wire rod from Japan.
Thailand's car production totalled roughly 590,000 units in 1996 and is expected to increase to 1.2 million units in 2000, Kobe added.
